headline: JEDEC releases SPHBM4 standard to slash AI memory costs with organic substrates
summary: The new SPHBM4 standard enables attaching HBM4 memory stacks without expensive interposers, utilizing a narrower 512-bit interface and standard organic substrates.
details: JEDEC has officially released its new SPHBM4 (Standard Package High Bandwidth Memory) specification, JESD330-4. This standard aims to significantly reduce the cost of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) used in advanced AI processors.

Unlike traditional HBM4, which requires expensive interposers and advanced packaging like TSMC's CoWoS, SPHBM4 utilizes a new PHY/buffer die. This allows for a narrower 512-bit interface, enabling integration with host processors using less-expensive organic substrates.

To compensate for the narrower interface, SPHBM4 supports considerably higher data transfer rates, ranging from 22.4 GT/s to 46.0 GT/s. It organizes 32 independent 16-bit DDR channels into eight 'Quad Channels' for efficient data flow.

The new base die incorporates a high-speed SerDes-like PHY, introducing features such as equalization, lane training, and BER requirements. Data transfers rely on dedicated differential write and read clocks, along with ECC and error-reporting signals.

SPHBM4 can support memory stacks with capacities up to 64 GB, built from sixteen 32 Gb DRAM dies, matching the maximum capacity of HBM4E. The standard allows for bump pitches greater than 90 µm and channel reaches up to 20 mm.

While SPHBM4 still requires massive HBM4 DRAM ICs and 2.5D packaging, the ability to drop expensive interposers and use organic substrates is a key cost-saving measure. Its narrower interface also consumes less die perimeter and silicon area on host processors, making it more attractive for integration.

headline_marked: Google releases [[Gemma 2]] LLMs with architectural tweaks for efficiency
headline: Google releases Gemma 2 LLMs with architectural tweaks for efficiency
summary: Google's new Gemma 2 models arrive in 9B and 27B parameter sizes, featuring architectural changes for improved inference efficiency and fine-tuning.
details: Google has launched Gemma 2, the latest iteration of its open large language model family, offering 9 billion and 27 billion parameter versions. These models are built with technology similar to Gemini and are designed for efficient deployment on hardware like a single NVIDIA H100 GPU or Google TPU host.

The 27B model is competitive with models twice its size, while the 9B model has also seen significant improvements. Both models were trained on massive datasets, with the 27B model processing 13 trillion tokens and the 9B model handling 8 trillion, both maintaining a 8192 token context length.

The core innovation in Gemma 2 lies in its architectural efficiency improvements. It utilizes a hybrid attention mechanism, alternating between local sliding window attention (4096 tokens) and global attention (full 8192 tokens) across different layers to manage long contexts more effectively.

Gemma 2 also incorporates Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) to reduce computational and memory overhead during inference, leading to faster performance and lower resource requirements without sacrificing quality. Additional features like logit soft-capping and RMSNorm further enhance stability.

These new models are accessible via Hugging Face, Kaggle, and Google AI Studio, with straightforward integration into frameworks like PyTorch and TensorFlow. Quantized versions are also available for reduced VRAM and memory footprints on consumer hardware.

Gemma 2 represents a significant step towards smaller, more efficient open models capable of rivaling larger proprietary systems. Its architectural design directly addresses the high inference costs, making it more feasible for teams to deploy custom-tuned, high-performance models without requiring massive GPU clusters.
